overall_rationale: All seven substantive Round-3 claim-scope, theorem, TV-geometry, protocol, and PDF checks pass for the compiled manuscript. checks.question: Does the compiled manuscript withdraw the per-K oracle profile as an executable/deployable/policy repair, a Theorem-1 instance, and a source of extra-vote/cost/70-of-72/universal-budget conclusions?
evidence: PDF pp.16-17, Appendix E(g), calls the object an 'oracle K-wise profile-capping sensitivity calculation' and says it is not the profile of one rule.
PDF p.17 states that final K is unobserved at every nonterminal prefix; there is neither a common S(x,k) nor agreement of K-indexed memberships on shared reachable states.

The same paragraph explicitly says 'not a stopping policy', 'not prefix-observable', and 'not an instance of Theorem 1'; it rejects executable/deployable repair, policy-level count/cost, extra-vote, universal-budget, 70-of-72, domination, edge-law, crossing-set, and full-simplex claims.

Active source manuscript/paper.tex:1167-1183 matches the PDF. Its required future condition is one K-independent prefix-observable S(x,k), a measurability check, and recomputed profiles plus capacity-aware TV LP.
The Round-2 adjudication found the K-indexed repair allegation valid while finding Theorem 1 independent of it; the active wording conforms to that ruling.
checks.qualification: Other active whole-simplex/TV statements concern a genuinely fixed prefix-measurable rule, not the withdrawn K-wise construction; they are not counterexamples to this withdrawal.
checks.minimal_remaining_action: None for the compiled claim boundary; remove the historical source block as specified in V06.

checks.question: Is K unobservability explicit and is the residual calculation only oracle sensitivity?

checks.question: Has the false global affine-TV identity been removed, and are the B_1 endpoint and general capacity-constrained piecewise-linear statements correct?
evidence: Active Proposition at manuscript/paper.tex:342-363 says the frozen-rule objective is a capacity-constrained LP, uses a capped two-sided greedy, is nondecreasing and piecewise linear in R, and is not generally globally affine because capacities create breakpoints.

The active-source audit passed 'tv-capacity-geometry' and 'oracle-policy-claims-withdrawn'; it strips only the marked historical conditional and confirms no active former prop:prefix label or base-affine formula.

Mathematical endpoint check: for probability vectors q and H-hat, ||q-H-hat||_1 is at most 2. Thus B_1 equals the entire simplex; maximizing the linear functional sum_K q_K g(K) over that simplex gives max_K g(K). This validates V(1)=max_K g(K).

The previous Proposition 2, its all-R formula V(R)=base+R(g_max-base), and its base-driven crossing conclusion occur only inside the source conditional at manuscript/paper.tex:939-1166 and are absent from the compiled PDF.
The Round-2 adjudication specifically prescribed this endpoint correction and warned against retaining the affine formula; the active proposition follows that prescription.
checks.qualification: The endpoint derivation is mathematically correct but terse in the manuscript ('Since B_1 is the full simplex').
checks.minimal_remaining_action: Optional clarity hardening: add one sentence showing ||q-H-hat||_1<=2 for two simplex points and that a linear maximum is at a simplex vertex; this is not a correctness blocker.

checks.question: Are Theorem 2's i.i.d., FIT/CAL independence, FIT freezing, and TEST-status conditions sufficiently explicit?
evidence: Theorem 2 (manuscript/paper.tex:315-335) assumes FIT and CAL are independent i.i.d. task samples from a common count-exchangeable replay population; conditional on FIT it freezes a finite pre-declared family including certificate tables; then it applies per-rule empirical Bernstein and Bonferroni over J frozen candidates.

Protocol text at manuscript/paper.tex:474-490 repeats i.i.d. sampling, FIT/CAL independence, freezing before CAL inspection, CAL-only selection, and that TEST is read once, excluded from selection, and descriptive rather than a second population guarantee.
The claim audit passed its 'cal-theorem-assumptions' check.

checks.question: Do title, abstract, and Table 1 identify the replay-only scope and CAL-versus-TEST status?
evidence: Title: 'Adaptive Stopping in Count-Exchangeable Binary Pass-Count Replay' (manuscript/paper.tex:35-37).

Abstract opens with count-exchangeable binary pass-count replay and closes by excluding delivered-answer majority, gold correctness, generated tokens, latency, cancellation, and ordered online deployment (lines 45-56 and 81-84).

Table 1 caption and status row (source lines 521-536; PDF p.7) call it a fixed-benchmark descriptive TEST readout, define CAL-selected as FIT-frozen CAL-UCB selection rather than a TEST guarantee, and label FULL/WINDOW3 as no-CAL-certificate references.
The claim audit passed 'headline-replay-scope' and 'table1-status'.

non_blocking_evidence_boundaries: An executable E(g) policy repair remains unproved until one K-independent observable state table is serialized, mechanically checked, and used to recompute profiles and the capacity-aware TV LP.

This verification does not close the existing absence of naturally ordered rollout traces, gold stopped-answer correctness, token/latency/cancellation telemetry, raw task/split/selection provenance, or an end-to-end environment lock. The active manuscript appropriately does not claim those endpoints.
